subject: Skylark trial: workload patterns, success criteria, and POC owners
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Leah Torres <leah@skylark.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + workload intake for the upcoming trial

Hi Leah —

Thanks for the productive call today. Below is a short recap and the information we need to kick off a focused POC. Goal is to have a small, repeatable test that demonstrates cost/latency characteristics for your core "recommendation" flow and validates quality thresholds.

What Redwood will demonstrate in the POC
- Baseline latency and 95/99p tail under your realistic concurrency and burst patterns
- Cost per 1k tokens under our default batching/caching profiles and a tuned config
- Stability during short bursts (2–5 minutes) and cold-start behavior

Required workload / traffic intake (please reply with these if you can):
1) Average sustained RPS (requests/sec) during business hours and off-peak
2) Peak burst RPS and typical burst duration
3) Average prompt length (tokens) and average model response length (tokens)
4) Concurrent active sessions or inference threads expected
5) Typical request distribution (percent of short prompts <64 tokens, 64-256, >256)
6) Any streaming/function-calling usage or long-living KV cache needs
7) PII/security constraints and S3/endpoint we can use for test data

Proposed success criteria (we can iterate):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms (token-generation latency) for typical prompts
- Quality: pass your sample prompt set with no more than 2% critical failures
- Reliability: <1% error rate during steady-state, automatic fallback for overloads

Initial timeline (flexible):
- 11/10 — kickoff & access handoff
- 11/11 — Redwood pulls sample traffic and validates onboarding
- 11/17 — baseline performance tests
- 11/24 — tuned config and final evaluation

Next steps for you: share the items in the intake list and the sample CSV (if available). If simpler, grant a temporary S3 read-only link and we’ll pull a sample. I’ve attached a short intake template to make the fields easy to fill.

Owners:
- Redwood: Monica (program lead), Rishi (contracts/credits), Dev (technical lead)
- Skylark: Leah (product), Caleb (infra)

Thanks — happy to hop on another 20-min call to walk through the intake. 

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_poc_intake_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Leah Torres <leah@skylark.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Caleb Ng <caleb@skylark.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + workload intake for the upcoming trial

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear list. Answers below and I attached a short sample export.

Quick answers:
1) Sustained RPS: ~20 RPS during business hours (09:00–18:00 PT), ~3 RPS off-peak
2) Peak bursts: we see spikes up to ~300 RPS for 2–5 minutes during campaign sends
3) Token lengths: avg prompt 110 tokens, avg response 140 tokens (we use a BPE tokenizer)
4) Concurrent active sessions: typically 15–30 concurrent inference threads
5) Distribution: ~40% <64, ~45% 64–256, ~15% >256
6) Streaming: we do not stream; we use function calls for a subset (about 12% of requests)
7) Security: PII redacted in sample. We can create a read-only S3 bucket for the trial and add redwood-poc@skylark as reader; will grant this during onboarding.

Success criteria: the suggested latency targets look good; we can relax 95p to 350ms if needed on day-0 but would like <250ms in tuned config. Error tolerance: <0.5% for user-facing failures.

Attaching: skylark_sample_traffic.csv (10k rows, anonymized)

Leah

Attachments: skylark_sample_traffic.csv (CSV)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Leah Torres <leah@skylark.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + workload intake for the upcoming trial

Great — thanks for the fast turnaround and the sample CSV, Leah.

I pulled the sample and shared a short plan below. Please confirm the access method (S3 link vs temporary credentials) and whether we should use a dedicated test account or a sandbox of your prod model.

Redwood POC plan (high level):
- 11/10 kickoff (30 min): confirm S3 & test credentials, share mapping of fields in CSV
- 11/11 data ingest & dry-run (Dev runs a smoke test against a pinned model)
- 11/17 baseline profile (run 3x 10-minute steady-state tests and 2x 3-minute burst tests)
- 11/20 tune config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization profile)
- 11/24 evaluation and handover with suggested production config

Owners & immediate asks:
- Dev Patel (redwood) — request S3 read-only link and example request JSON from your side by EOD 11/09
- Rishi Malhotra (redwood) — will prepare credit/discount paperwork and contract addendum
- Leah (skylark) — confirm SSO/test account preference and grant the S3 link

Notes for Dev (technical): we saw 300 RPS bursts in the CSV. For the POC recommend we run
- steady-state: 20 RPS for 10 minutes
- burst test: ramp to 300 RPS for 3 minutes
- sample prompt lengths: use the distribution Leah provided

Attaching: redwood_poc_intake_template.xlsx

If that timeline works, I’ll send a calendar invite for 11/10 kickoff. 

Best,
Monica

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Leah Torres <leah@skylark.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + workload intake for the upcoming trial

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:22 AM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com> wrote:
> Notes for Dev (technical): we saw 300 RPS bursts in the CSV. For the POC recommend we run
> - steady-state: 20 RPS for 10 minutes
> - burst test: ramp to 300 RPS for 3 minutes
> - sample prompt lengths: use the distribution Leah provided

Quick clarifying items from my side before the kickoff:
- Tokenization: are you providing prompts pre-tokenized or should Redwood run the same BPE tokenizer? (We prefer to match exactly.)
- Max sequence length we should provision for (prompt + response). Leah listed >256 for 15% — do you have a hard max?
- Function calls: for the ~12% of requests that use function calling, do you expect synchronous returns or async webhooks? We need that to size client-side concurrency.
- KV cache: any expectation of long-term KV cache reuse per session (helps reduce cost for multi-turn flows)

If you can add one sample raw request JSON and one function-call example to the S3 bucket, that would remove guesswork.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com

From: Leah Torres <leah@skylark.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Caleb Ng <caleb@skylark.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + workload intake for the upcoming trial

Thanks Dev — answers inline:

- Tokenization: please run Redwood’s tokenizer but use our provided vocabulary file (pushed to S3 under /tokenizer/vocab.json). We want exact parity for quality checks.
- Max sequence: maximum observed ~1024 tokens; we rarely exceed 1200 but you can cap at 1024 for the POC and flag any longer examples.
- Function calls: synchronous responses (return payload in the response) for POC; we’ll test webhooks in phase 2.
- KV cache: yes — per-session cache with TTL of 30 minutes for the multi-turn flows (helps hit rate for follow-ups).

I’ve added two files to the S3 bucket:
- skylark_sample_traffic.csv (already shared)
- skylark_example_requests.json (three anonymized request examples including a function-call example)

Security contact is security@skylark.ai if you need SOC/Security docs. We’ll create the redwood-poc@skylark read-only role and email creds by EOD.

Leah
Product Manager | Skylark AI

Attachments: skylark_poc_s3_readme.txt
